title: Signatech Alpine passes Jota late to win at the Red Bull Ring
dek: Oliver Webb took the lead for Signatech Alpine from pole-sitting Jota's Simon Dolan after the final stops and won the 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring by 12.385 seconds.

chapters.title: Two months on, the field is thinner
text: The third round of the 2014 European Le Mans Series, the 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 20 July, came after a two-month break that had included the Le Mans 24 Hours. The LMP2 title fight was open: Jota Sport had won at Imola in May, while Thiriet by TDS Racing led the points table. Signatech Alpine, the reigning champions, had yet to win in 2014 but had found their feet on Dunlop tyres at Imola.

The class shrank to eight cars. Sébastien Loeb Racing and Murphy Prototypes both pulled their Oreca-Nissans out in the days before the race, and Larbre Competition's Morgan was absent as well. The biggest line-up change was at Newblood by Morand Racing, where Pierre Ragues took the seat vacated by Romain Brandela alongside Christian Klien, racing on home soil, and Gary Hirsch. Greaves Motorsport ran two Zytek-Nissans again after a single-car entry at Imola, with Mark Patterson joining Tom Kimber-Smith and Matthew Mcmurry in the #41, and Luciano Bacheta making his prototype debut alongside Mark Shulzhitskiy in the #28. The Thiriet by TDS Ligier JS P2 was the only closed-cockpit car in the class, and Pegasus Racing brought a single Morgan-Nissan of its two.

The weekend was hot, with track temperatures in the high 30s on Saturday and more of the same forecast for the race. Free practice was tight at the front. Michel Frey put the Race Performance Oreca-Judd on top in the morning, then Klien's Morgan-Judd set 1:24.145 in the second session, 0.008 seconds clear of Franck Mailleux and 0.064 ahead of the Thiriet Ligier. Saturday evening brought the stewards into play: Nelson Panciatici was reprimanded for improving his time under yellow flags in the second session, and given a suspended exclusion from the meeting that would apply if he repeated the offence.

chapters.title: Tincknell completes a hat-trick for Jota
text: Harry Tincknell took pole for Jota Sport with 1:23.078 on his final lap. It was the team's third pole in a row, and the second of the season for Tincknell himself. "We've got qualifying down to a 't' at present," he said, and he confirmed that Filipe Albuquerque would start the race.

Franck Mailleux was second for Race Performance, 0.483 seconds adrift (1:23.561), setting his time on his last lap. Tristan Gommendy had traded times with Tincknell and was on provisional pole with three minutes left, but chose to save his Dunlops for the race and ended up third on 1:23.613, just over half a second off the top.

Klien was fourth for Newblood by Morand (1:23.763), a little short of the top three, and Panciatici fifth for Signatech Alpine, who had led early on. Kimber-Smith edged Bacheta for sixth and seventh, both Greaves cars within a couple of thousandths of each other (1:23.995 and 1:23.997). Julien Schell was eighth in the Pegasus Morgan on 1:25.449, about a second and a half behind the next car.

chapters.title: Albuquerque leads, Thiriet's day ends early
text: Albuquerque started the pole-sitting Jota Zytek and led from the first lap, with Frey in the Race Performance Oreca-Judd tracking him. A Safety Car came out about seven minutes in to recover the Team Russia by Barwell BMW. The neutralisation cost Albuquerque some seconds of his advantage, but at the restart he pulled them out again and was soon about seven seconds clear of Frey.

Further back, Pierre Thiriet and Ragues had a spirited fight in the opening exchanges before the Thiriet by TDS Ligier suffered a brake disc failure. A broken axle followed and the car was out after 40 laps, the only LMP2 retirement and a heavy blow to the team that led the points table going into the weekend.

chapters.title: Dolan leads, Chatin takes over
text: Albuquerque handed over to Simon Dolan, who rejoined behind Frey's Oreca. Frey had lost ground on soft Dunlops late in a long opening double stint, and Dolan caught and passed him to retake the lead. Gary Hirsch then pressed the Jota Zytek for a time, but the Newblood by Morand Morgan lost time when Ragues stopped on pit entry. Hirsch had to serve a stop-and-go penalty, and the team collected three penalties in all over the race.

Signatech Alpine came into the picture during the second hour. Paul-Loup Chatin got his Alpine A450b alongside Dolan in a duel between the two silver-rated drivers and took the lead after the second round of pit stops. Tincknell took over from Dolan with roughly an hour and a half to go and set about the Frenchman, who was eight seconds up the road; Chatin kept the faster Zytek behind him for a long time with a series of strong laps. Elsewhere, the Pegasus Morgan lost a long stretch in the pits and was classified 29th overall, 18 laps down.

chapters.title: Webb's move decides it
text: With about an hour left Tincknell finally got through, passing Chatin only to see him fight straight back. Tincknell passed again and began to build a gap, roughly six seconds, for Dolan, who had to complete a minimum driving time in the last stint. It was not enough. Signatech turned its car around faster than Jota at the final stops, and Dolan rejoined just a couple of car lengths ahead of Oliver Webb.

Webb outdragged the Zytek out of the second corner a lap later, passing for the lead with 42 minutes remaining, and then pulled clear. The Alpine was 12.385 seconds ahead at the flag after 160 laps. Frey and Mailleux, whose Race Performance Oreca had been compromised early, closed to within a few seconds of the Jota in the final stint and completed the podium, 18.772 seconds behind the winners. Mailleux also set the fastest lap of the race, 1:24.969.

Bacheta and Shulzhitskiy took fourth for Greaves, 51.412 seconds behind, a strong result for Bacheta on his prototype debut. Klien took fifth for Newblood by Morand, two laps down, after a long fight with Kimber-Smith, whose Greaves finished sixth, also two laps off the lead.

chapters.title: Signatech Alpine takes the points lead
text: It was Signatech Alpine's first victory of 2014 and moved the defending champions to the top of the LMP2 standings, ahead of Jota Sport. Panciatici, Chatin and Webb scored 50 points to Jota's 46, with Race Performance on 39 and the Thiriet by TDS Ligier, which had led going into the weekend, down to fourth on 35. Webb called it his first win with Alpine and said the pit stops had been perfect, adding that the team would spend the summer as leaders. Panciatici said the team had to seize its chance to stay in the title fight, which was the team's clear aim.

Team boss Philippe Sinault credited Chatin: "Paul-Loup's pace was the key to our victory today." Chatin had kept Tincknell behind for long enough that Jota had few laps to build a cushion before the last stops. Albuquerque, who had driven the opening stint, accepted that Jota could not win every time, and said the championship would be very tight for everybody.

For Jota, second place still gave the team a good result after three successive poles, and Tincknell had already pointed out that the extra pole points could matter at the end of the year. Race Performance's podium repaired some of the early-season promise that had faded since the spring, and Greaves had both cars in the top six. Newblood by Morand finished fifth despite its penalties and the lost lap, a recovery for a team whose Imola race had ended with Klien stopping from the lead in the closing minutes.

Series CEO Gérard Neveu said he expected the class fights to go down to the finale at Estoril in October, where the 2015 calendar was due to be announced. The series next heads to Paul Ricard in the weekend of 13 and 14 September, with the LMP2 title still wide open between four teams within 15 points of each other.

facts.v: Oliver Webb passed Simon Dolan for the lead with 42 minutes left and won by 12.385 seconds after 160 laps.
Harry Tincknell took pole with 1:23.078, 0.483 seconds ahead of Franck Mailleux, for Jota Sport's third pole in a row.
The win put Signatech Alpine on 50 points, four ahead of Jota Sport on 46, with Race Performance third on 39.
